Class Launcher

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.Launcher
public final class Launcher extends Object
The Main-Class of every runner jar.

Starting an application is four steps: find the archive this class was loaded from, map it, read its index, and hand both to a RunnerClassLoader. The application is then entered either through the Entry the packager generated - an invokeinterface, with no reflection and no method handle anywhere on the path - or, when no stub could be generated, through the reflective fallback that implements the same main method selection rules as the java launcher.

What this class deliberately does not do

  • It does not close the ArchiveSource or the Index. Application threads keep loading classes long after main returns, so the mapping has to outlive it; the process exit releases it.
  • It does not catch the application's exceptions or install a shutdown hook. A Throwable out of the application propagates out of main(String[]) unchanged, so the JVM prints it and sets the exit status exactly as it would for an ordinary main class.

Exit codes

0 when the application returns normally, 1 when it throws - that is the JVM's own behaviour for an uncaught exception - and 2 for a launcher level failure such as a missing, unreadable or stale archive, which is reported on standard error and never as a stack trace.

    • register

      public static void register(Entry registration)
      Registers the application entry point. The class the packager generates calls this from its static initialiser, so that the launcher can enter the application through an interface call.
      Parameters:
      registration - the entry point
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the entry point is null
      IllegalStateException - if an entry point is already registered; a runner jar starts once per JVM
